note: He describes himself in almost exactly the ICP's own words - 'I don't have, you know, 50 pounds to lose, I'm already in, you know, fairly good shape, I'm just wanting to fine-tune everything' - so good_to_great and not_deconditioned are unambiguous. Successful holds on a loose reading: a self-employed tattoo artist with a growing fitness following, deliberately transitioning to fewer client days and building an online coaching business. Income is inferred rather than tested; he asked for monthly payments by preference rather than constraint and paid $1,200 on the call. The single miss is the one the ICP quote leans on hardest: health is not the neglected area of his life, it is the best-developed part of it and about to become his profession. He trains six to seven times a week, stays lean, tracks calories and already writes programmes for other people. That miss matters commercially, because what he actually wants is knowledge transfer rather than transformation, and it is why the six-month structure did not survive contact with him.
